clue.text: Intellectual bloke originally in wrong career left

indicators.note: in means the bloke's first letter is placed inside the jumbled word
wrong means the letters of career are put in the wrong order
originally means only the first letter of bloke is taken

explanation.surface: A clever man who started out in the wrong career has now quit it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' scrambles CAREER into CERERA, 'originally' takes B from bloke, and 'in' puts it inside to make CEREBRA, followed by L.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerebral describes someone brainy and drawn to thought, a synonym of intellectual.

clue.text: Concealment of truth about entering competition

indicators.note: entering means the word for about goes inside the word for competition

parts.note: a cup is a competition, as in the FA Cup
over can mean about, as in arguing over money

explanation.surface: Someone hides the facts about getting into a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Hiding the facts of a scandal is the classic whitewash, a synonym for this hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Ran a church in outskirts of Romford

indicators.note: in means the letters for a church sit inside the outer letters of the town
outskirts of means only the first and last letters of Romford are used

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone sprinted to a church on the edge of Romford, a town in east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Romford is a town on the eastern edge of London; its first and last letters are R and D.
explanation.definitionFit: Raced is the past tense of race, meaning moved fast, the same as ran.

clue.text: Dog tethered around something good and hard

indicators.note: around means the word for tethered encloses the other pieces

parts.note: bound means tied up, tethered
an asset is a useful or valuable thing
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dog on a lead is wrapped round something nice and solid.
explanation.definitionFit: This long-eared, short-legged hound is a breed of dog used for tracking.

clue.text: Tech company last to document program

parts.note: Apple is the American technology firm behind the iPhone

indicators.note: last to means just the final letter of document is taken

explanation.surface: A tech firm is the last one to write up its software.
explanation.definitionFit: An applet is a small application, a type of computer program that runs inside another.

clue.text: Plant, one beside river

parts.note: an ace is a one in a pack of cards
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A single plant grows beside the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, so it names a tree or plant.

clue.text: Pairs of two-door cars, about 50

indicators.note: about means the word for the cars goes round the Roman numeral

parts.note: coupes are two-door cars with a fixed roof
L is fifty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Sets of two-door sports cars number roughly fifty.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples are twos, items that come in twos, the same as pairs.

clue.text: Irritable being restrained by autocrat tyrannically

indicators.note: being restrained by means the answer is held inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone becomes cross while held down by a cruel dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty is British slang for bad-tempered and snappish, a synonym for irritable.

clue.text: Expressed opinions to reject love for immoral habits

indicators.note: to reject means the letter for love is thrown out of the longer word

parts.note: voices as a verb means expresses opinions, as in voiced concerns
love means nil in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: People spoke out to reject affection in favour of wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Vices are wicked or bad practices, the opposite of virtues.

clue.text: Something made for channel

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a duct is a tube or channel carrying liquid or air

explanation.surface: Something was built for a canal.
explanation.definitionFit: A product is an item manufactured or produced.

clue.text: Ignorant men destroyed decking

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters of these two words are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Uneducated men wrecked a wooden patio.
explanation.definitionFit: Decking can mean adorning, as in decking the halls, so it means decorating.

clue.text: Listened to learned socialist

indicators.note: listened to means the word for learned is heard spoken rather than seen

parts.note: read, past tense, means studied or learned, as in she read law

explanation.surface: Someone heard a well-educated left-winger.
explanation.definitionFit: Red is a long-standing label for a communist or left-winger.

clue.text: Always eating at front, seabird and mate

indicators.note: at front means only the opening letter of eating is wanted

parts.note: a tern is a slender gull-like seabird
an ally is a friend or partner, a mate

explanation.surface: A seabird and its partner are forever eating at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means for ever, without end, a synonym for always.

clue.text: Power to shed illumination on predicament

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
to light something is to shed illumination on it

explanation.surface: Power is needed to shine a lamp on a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or difficult situation, the same as a predicament.

clue.text: Guaranteed US diner needs renovating

indicators.note: needs renovating means the letters of US diner are rebuilt in another order

explanation.surface: An American roadside restaurant needs a refit.
explanation.definitionFit: Insured means covered by a policy, protected against loss, so guaranteed.

clue.text: Pleasantly occupied in the morning, exercised

parts.note: AM is short for ante meridiem, before noon
to exercise a right is to use it, so exercised can mean used

explanation.surface: Someone happily spent the morning working out.
explanation.definitionFit: Amused means entertained, kept agreeably busy.

clue.text: Ridicules of French fairground attractions

parts.note: de is the French word for of
rides such as dodgems and the big wheel are fairground attractions

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the French funfair.
explanation.definitionFit: Derides means mocks or scorns, a synonym for ridicules.

clue.text: Newspaper boss rejected rubbish I would write, ultimately

indicators.note: rejected means the whole string of pieces is sent back the other way

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: ultimately means only the final letter of write is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper chief turns down nonsense that someone would finally write.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole run ROT + ID + E backwards; reading it from the end gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is the person in charge of a newspaper's content.

clue.text: Unload bus ridden round the bend

indicators.note: round the bend is slang for mad, so these letters are crazily rearranged

explanation.surface: Empty the bus that has been driven round the corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round the bend' looks like a route but is British slang for crazy, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To disburden is to free from a load, so it means unload.

clue.text: Transport leaving back of major warehouse

indicators.note: leaving means the chosen letter departs from the word for transport

parts.note: to deport someone is to transport them out of a country

indicators.note: back of means the last letter of major

explanation.surface: Transport departs from the rear of a large storehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes R, the final letter of major, and 'leaving' takes it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse for goods, a warehouse.

clue.text: Rattle glass container

explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to jolt or shake, to rattle; a jar is also a glass pot for jam or pickles.

clue.text: Just half gone, cool drink

indicators.note: half gone means only the first half of just survives

parts.note: ice cools, and to ice is to chill

explanation.surface: Just half finished, a chilled beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Juice is a drink pressed from fruit.

clue.text: Gemstone salesperson turned over with one circular symbol

indicators.note: turned over means the word for salesperson is flipped backwards

parts.note: rep is short for sales representative
I is the Roman numeral one
a dot is a small round mark

explanation.surface: A salesman flipped a single round mark onto a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is a green gemstone, a form of the mineral olivine.

clue.text: War poem reflected injured ailing somewhat

indicators.note: reflected means the letters run back as in a mirror
somewhat means only part of the words injured ailing is taken

explanation.surface: A war poem reflects the wounded and the somewhat sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' takes DAILI from the middle of injureD AILIng, and 'reflected' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's epic about the siege of Troy is the most famous war poem.

clue.text: Starters of ten individual dips you ordered

indicators.note: starters of means the first letters of the next four words

explanation.surface: Ten single snacks you requested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like requested, part of a meal order, but here it means arranged neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy describes something neat and in order.

clue.text: Ill-tempered people in sports regularly advance

indicators.note: in means the word for ill-tempered people sits inside the picked letters
regularly means every other letter of sports is taken

parts.note: ogres are brutish, bad-tempered people

explanation.surface: Grumpy people in sport keep moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes P, R and S, the second, fourth and sixth letters of sports; OGRES goes between R and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Progress means move forward, to advance.
